tokens.styling: TCSS (.tcss files, hot-reloadable): real selectors (type/#id/.class/pseudo), theme tokens $primary/$surface/$error, built-in themes (textual-dark, nord, gruvbox, dracula, catppuccin)
tokens.layout: TCSS layouts: vertical/horizontal/grid (grid-size, spans)/dock (pin header/footer/sidebar)/layers (z-order overlays); units cells/%/fr/auto

components.name: Button / Input
components.when_to_use: actions and text fields (MaskedInput for masked)

components.name: Log / RichLog
components.when_to_use: streaming logs (Log = fast plain, RichLog = any Rich renderable)

rules: Never block the event loop (the top bug) — use @work / @work(thread=True); @work(exclusive=True) for search-as-you-type.
Do setup in on_mount, not compose (compose must be fast/side-effect-free); query_one fails before mount.
Put styling in .tcss with IDs/classes (not inline styles.*); handle messages with @on(Widget.Event, "#id").
Update widgets from threads via call_from_thread. Use Textual for interactive multi-screen apps; Rich alone for one-shot/streamed formatted output.
Textual ships a Python runtime (no single binary) and is single-maintainer post-Textualize (still MIT/active) — weigh that on multi-year bets; textual-serve gives the same app in a browser.
